title: Whales in the Sea of Cortez
coverImageAlt: Wildlife placeholder — real whale photography to come
excerpt: The first blow came up about two hundred meters off the bow, and everyone on deck went quiet at the same time.
subtitle: Humpbacks move through the Sea of Cortez every winter, and some years they come closer to La Paz than anyone plans for.
author: Flavia Ibarra
body:
We'd cut the engine to drift near Isla Espíritu Santo when someone spotted the spray. Humpbacks pass through the Sea of Cortez from December through April, working their way south from feeding grounds in the north Pacific, and most years a few pass close enough to the boat to change the plan for the day.

The rule on board is simple: if a whale shows up, the itinerary waits. We cut the engine, keep our distance, and let the animal decide how close it wants to get. Sometimes that's not very close at all.

> You can hear a humpback breathe before you see it. The sound carries further than you'd think across flat water.

![Placeholder — real photo of dolphins on the crossing back to La Paz to come](/assets/img/hero-premium.webp "Dolphins joined for part of the crossing back to La Paz.")

By the time the whale sounded, the light was starting to go gold, which is the other reason nobody was in a hurry to get back.

We anchored that night at Espíritu Santo instead of finishing the loop back to the marina. Nobody on board complained about the change of plan.
